title: Droppen hub API v1: HTTP bodies
description: Look up a route as $defs["<METHOD> <path template>"]; its $defs hold `request` (the JSON body sent), `response` (the JSON body of a 2xx answer) and, where it differs from #/$defs/error, `error` (the body of any other answer). Templates are the ones in docs/hub-api/index.json. Every object may carry fields not listed here: /v1/ only grows, and a client must ignore what it does not know. Binary fields are lower-case hex.

releaseFile.description: One file of the latest release (GET /v1/releases/latest): its exact name, its address on GitHub (https://github.com/getdroppen/droppen/releases/download/<tag>/<name>) and its size in bytes.

relayPrefs.description: The account's relay preferences (relay-and-plans §2.7): `standby`, whether the hub keeps a standby relay in the account's set (two instead of one). Absent from /v1/me on hubs before it.

hex32.description: 32 bytes: a key, a nonce, a hash

b64url.description: base64url without padding: WebAuthn's own JSON encoding, used for the passkey routes' binary values (and only there)

challenge.description: A passkey ceremony's challenge (42 bytes, base64url): stateless, good for 2 minutes, answered once. Send it back exactly as given.

removalGrant.description: DELETE /v1/passkeys/{id}'s grant (42 bytes, base64url), given with 409 unlock_on after a proof: finishes removing that passkey from that device once the passkey slot naming it is off. Stateless, good for 2 minutes, taken once. Send it back exactly as given.

registrationResponse.description: WebAuthn's RegistrationResponseJSON (what PublicKeyCredential.toJSON() gives after create()). Of clientExtensionResults the hub reads only prf.enabled; send no more than credProps.rk and prf.enabled, never prf.results.

authenticationResponse.description: WebAuthn's AuthenticationResponseJSON (PublicKeyCredential.toJSON() after get()). userHandle is required for a sign-in: passkeys here are discoverable.

id.description: An account, device, machine or pairing id: 1-64 printable ASCII characters

limitValue.description: An entitlement's value; null: no limit

error.description: Every hub error: a stable machine-readable `error` code and a human `message`. 429s add `retry_after_ms` (and a Retry-After header); 409 `limit` adds the entitlement `key`, its `limit` and what is `used`; 409 `unlock_on` from DELETE /v1/passkeys/{id}, after a password or passkey proof, adds a removal `grant`.

relayError.description: A relay's error: `message` is absent on its 429 (`{error: "rate", retry_after_ms}`).

signedIn.description: A login session: good for 15 minutes, for POST /v1/devices, GET /v1/me, GET /v1/chain and POST /v1/logout only.

known_client.description: kc1.<account>.<expires_ms>.<tag>: send it with this client's next login (30 days); opaque to clients

planView.description: The account's plan, entitlements and usage (GET /v1/me `plan`; also a device's `plan` control message `detail`).

devices.description: Current devices of the chain, hosts included (counted against devices.max).

hosts.description: Current devices that run AI (counted against hosts.max). Since chain v3; `machines` is its old name, kept one version.

machine.description: A current host of the account's chain, or null: none

set_ms.description: When it was last set or cleared (ms); null: never

rotation.description: A host's identity key renewal (docs/host-identity-rotation.md §3.3): its state, what was asked, the staging (and, committed, the new keys), why it last failed, and what the hub holds against the host.

assurance.description: 1: confirmed on the device (the code typed in)

requested_by.description: the admin device that asked, or `hub` (isolated by evidence)

staged_ms.description: staged: when the host staged it

ready_ms.description: staged: when it may be committed (T after staged_ms, later while a sign-in still owes its confirmation)

sign_key.description: staged or committed: the new Ed25519 key

dh_key.description: staged or committed: the new X25519 key

staged_seq.description: staged or committed: the chain view the proof was made against

nonce_hash.description: attempt or staged: the SHA-256 of that attempt's nonce, as PUT took it — what names it to DELETE

reason.description: not_acked, conflict: clone evidence; interrupted (gone before it answered, or the hub's own error), replaced (the agent connection replaced during an attempt): no evidence — ask again with a fresh nonce; a second within a day is not_acked

needs_assurance.description: only a renewal confirmed on the device is taken: clone evidence within 30 days, or isolated (an account that always asks is the chain's own rule, SetRenewalPolicy)

isolated.description: a key a renewal not confirmed on the device retired was used again, and no renewal confirmed on the device came since: no relay tickets to or for it and no channel, but from an admin device (and its own agent's tickets) while an assurance-1 attempt or staging is open

rotationDispute.description: Evidence that someone else holds a host's key. A `disputed` statement (the only kind that isolates) carries {seq, entry_hash, sig}: the retired key's rh/v1 rotate-dispute signature over the renewal at seq, which a device checks with ChainState::verify_rotate_dispute on its own chain. A retired_login carries the signed login as it came: rh_proto::sig::HubLogin {role, account, id, hub, nonce, time_ms}, checked with sig against the chain's keys_at(host, retired_seq - 1).

retired_seq.description: retired_login: the renewal that retired the key

role.description: retired_login: the login's role (HubLogin Agent, Device, DeviceSession)

sig.description: disputed: the statement's signature; retired_login: the login's

sign_key.description: the retired key that signed it

isolates.description: disputed: whether it isolates the host (a renewal not confirmed on the device, none confirmed after it)

evidence.description: retired_login: whether it counts as clone evidence (needs_assurance); false for a sign-in to a challenge issued before the key's retirement or within 10 s after it (the host racing its own commit): information only

proof.description: Proof it is still the person (http.md, "The account's ways to sign in"): the current password (only where the account has one), or a passkey of the account's answering a challenge POST /v1/passkeys/reauth/options gave this device

reauthPasskey.description: Proof it is still the person: one of the account's passkeys answering a challenge POST /v1/passkeys/reauth/options gave this device

passkey.description: One of the account's passkeys (GET /v1/passkeys): nothing here is a secret

label.description: Its provider's name by AAGUID when added, else Passkey; renamed with PATCH

provider.description: Its provider's name by AAGUID, else Passkey

cred_hash.description: SHA-256 of the credential id: what a passkey slot on the chain names (docs/passkeys.md §4.2)

backup_eligible.description: BE: it may sync (a passkey manager's, not a security key's)

backup_state.description: BS: it does sync, as of its last use

prf.description: Whether the browser said it can do PRF when it was made: a hint only

created_by.description: The device that added it; null for one made at sign-up

unlock.description: on: a current passkey slot on the account's chain names it, so a new device can join with it

invite.description: Required with DROPPEN_HUB_SIGNUP=invite; at most 128 bytes once trimmed

email.description: The e-mail the options were asked for (the challenge is bound to it)

commit.description: the commit the hub's image was built from, when it knows

digest.description: sha256 of one `<sha256>  <path>\n` line per file of the build as written, sorted by path bytewise (docs/web-integrity.md)

response.description: The latest public release of getdroppen/droppen as the hub last read it from GitHub and checked: published, not a prerelease, tagged vX.Y.Z; only the files below, under their exact names. A platform whose file the release lacks is absent.

fetched_ms.description: When the hub read it (ms since the epoch); after a failed read the last good answer is served on.

passkeys.description: Passkeys offered, for this relying party id (docs/passkeys.md §3.1); null when the hub has them off. Absent from hubs before passkeys.

known_client.description: The known-client token an earlier sign-in to this account gave this client

passkey.description: The passkey that signed in: the hub's id, its label, and whether a current passkey slot on the account's chain names it (unlock on: a new device can join with it; a hint — the device goes by the chain it verifies). paused and none are not sent any more

request.description: Nothing: the passkey says whose it is

options.description: PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptionsJSON: challenge, rpId, timeout 120000, userVerification required, allowCredentials [] (any of the account's passkeys)

purpose.description: signup: create an account with a passkey (adding one to an account: POST /v1/passkeys/add/options)

invite.description: Required with DROPPEN_HUB_SIGNUP=invite; at most 128 bytes once trimmed

turnstile.description: The widget's token, when the hub uses Turnstile

options.description: PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptionsJSON: rp {id, name}, user {id, name, displayName}, challenge, pubKeyCredParams (-8, -7, -257), timeout 120000, authenticatorSelection {residentKey: required, userVerification: required}, attestation none, excludeCredentials, extensions {credProps, prf.eval.first}

email.description: Trimmed and lower-cased; one @, at most 64 bytes before it, a domain of two or more host labels

locale.description: The page's language; kept as one of en, zh-CN, zh-TW, ja

response.description: The same whether the address is new or already on the list

kind.description: As registered (metadata only); absent from hubs before local sign-in

host.description: As registered (metadata only); absent from hubs before local sign-in

ua_label.description: The device's browser by a short name, from the User-Agent of its own requests: "<device> · <browser>" or either alone, words of a fixed list only, never the User-Agent itself (metadata only); an iPad asking for desktop sites is "Mac" until its page asks for GET /v1/me?touch=1; null until one named something known; absent from hubs before it

reads_v3.description: Its agent last declared `chain/3` and `policy/1`. Absent from hubs before chain v3.

rotates.description: Its agent last declared `rotate/1`: it can renew its identity key. Absent from hubs before renewals.

chain_v3.description: Chain v3 (docs/local-aggregator.md §3.5): `mode` is the hub's DROPPEN_HUB_CHAIN_V3; `writable` says the account takes v3 entries now; `waiting` lists the current hosts whose agents have not declared `chain/3` and `policy/1`; `in_use` says the chain holds a v3 entry. Absent from hubs before chain v3.

rotations.description: Identity key renewals (docs/host-identity-rotation.md): whether this hub takes them, T, and each host's state (GET /v1/rotations has the rest). Absent from hubs before renewals.

known_client.description: Device sessions only: a fresh known-client token (as a sign-in's), to keep for this account's next password login

credentials.description: What the account signs in with: whether it has a password (an account made with a passkey has none), and how many passkeys. Absent from hubs before passkeys.

sign_in_changes.description: How the account's sign-in changed in the last 30 days, oldest first, at most the newest 50: each as the websocket's sign_in_changed says it (without `t`). Absent from hubs before it.

device.description: The device session that made the change

label.description: The passkey's label (the new one, for a rename); null for the password

kind.description: What the device is, e.g. "aggregator" (a computer's limited device). Metadata only.

host.description: The machine an aggregator runs on. Metadata only.

agents.description: machine id -> relay id -> round trip in ms, as each machine last reported

standby.description: Keep a standby relay: the hub keeps two relays in the account's set instead of one (relay.max allowing)

if_unset.description: Write only while the account has none (never set, or it left the account)

now_ms.description: the hub's clock: every age here is measured against it

disputes.description: the last 90 days' evidence, newest first, at most 100 — and always every dispute a still-isolated host's isolation rests on, however old

nonce_hash.description: SHA-256 of the request's 16-byte nonce: open an attempt. Without it: mark the host pending

request.description: Optional (no body: withdraw whatever the host has). At most one of the two: what is withdrawn, so that what another page started on the host since stays (409 rotation_in_progress while an attempt or staging is open, `{}` when the one named is gone)

nonce_hash.description: only the attempt (or staging) opened with this nonce hash

requested_ms.description: only the pending mark made then (`requested_ms` of the row)

POST /v1/rotations/{host}/disputes.description: No session: the retired key's signature is the credential.

sig.description: rh/v1 rotate-dispute by the sign key that renewal retired

password.description: Whether the account has a password

max.description: How many passkeys the account may have at once

options.description: PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptionsJSON as POST /v1/passkeys/options gives it, under the account's own user handle (user.id) and with the account's passkeys in excludeCredentials

label.description: 1–64 characters once trimmed, no control characters; absent: the provider's name
1–64 characters once trimmed, no control characters

request.description: Proof it is still the person (as #/$defs/proof), or instead the grant a 409 unlock_on gave this device for this passkey
Nothing: the device session says whose account and which device

options.description: PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptionsJSON: challenge, rpId, timeout 120000, userVerification required, allowCredentials the account's own passkeys (type, id, transports)

current_password.description: Proof it is still the person, where the account has a password: that password

GET /v1/relay-id.description: Served by a relay, asked by the hub when the relay registers or moves (query: nonce=<64 hex>).

GET /v1/ping.description: Served by a relay: 204, no body.

GET /v1/connect.description: Served by a relay: the WebSocket upgrade; refused with a 429 when the address is over its limit.
